details.description: FLUX.1 Kontext [pro] is Black Forest Labs' production-tier image generation and editing model that unifies text-to-image generation with in-context, instruction-based image editing in a single model. Per Black Forest Labs' documentation, it targets fast, iterative editing workflows, preserving character consistency across multiple edit turns while supporting both targeted local edits and full-scene transformations. Black Forest Labs' current developer docs now recommend FLUX.2 over FLUX.1 Kontext for new projects, citing higher resolution (up to 4MP) and multi-reference support, positioning Kontext as a previous-generation model that remains available via its API.
advantages: Supports iterative, multi-turn editing while preserving character consistency across edits, per Black Forest Labs' documentation.
Handles both targeted local edits and full text-to-image generation in a single unified model, per Black Forest Labs' documentation.
Accepts input images up to 20MB or 20 megapixels and supports aspect ratios from 3:7 to 7:3, per Black Forest Labs' documentation.
disadvantages: Black Forest Labs now recommends FLUX.2 over FLUX.1 Kontext for new image generation and editing projects, citing higher resolution (up to 4MP) and multi-reference support.
Outputs are limited to roughly 1 megapixel total resolution, per Black Forest Labs' documentation.
Black Forest Labs positions the Kontext [max] tier above Kontext [pro] for prompt adherence and typography generation, per Black Forest Labs' documentation.
use_cases: Fast, iterative text-to-image generation and editing
Targeted local edits to specific regions of an existing image
Full scene transformation from a text prompt and a reference image

notes: Catalog's modality for this Fireworks entry lists text_input/image_output only, but Black Forest Labs documents Kontext as taking both a text prompt and an input image for editing; kept the catalog's modality per instructions. Found no accuracy-style (0-100, higher-is-better) benchmark scores for this exact model — Black Forest Labs' own comparisons are ranking/Elo-style across evaluation tasks, which the evaluations rules exclude, so the list is left empty. No prices are stated despite Black Forest Labs' docs quoting a per-image price, per instructions to omit prices.
